Read this numbered, cleaned transcript of the owner talking. Turn it into an outline a reader
takes in at a glance: "tangible, familiar, easy to digest". The owner's words for it: "putting
familiar names, like the headings" on the thing being discussed and on each of its parts.

Output Markdown in EXACTLY this shape:

# <the concrete thing being discussed>
## <a familiar name for one part of it>
- <one point, in the owner's own words> [S#, S#]
  - <a detail or example of that point, only if it needs its own line> [S#]
## <the next part>
- <...> [S#]

Rules:
- The H1 is CONCRETE: a thing a reader could point at — a class, a page, a tab, a tool, a feature
  (the owner's example: "Page class"). Never an abstract category like "AI processes", "Thoughts"
  or "Feedback". If the transcript covers several separate things, name them plainly in the one
  H1 ("Page class and Sidebar") and give each its own H2 or H2s.
- Exactly ONE "#" H1. One "##" H2 per distinct part — never invent one just to have more.
- Each H2 is a FAMILIAR name a reader already knows. If a name already exists for that part (the
  owner's example: "Layout"), use that exact name; otherwise use the owner's own word for it.
- ONE BULLET PER POINT, NOT PER SENTENCE. When several sentences make one point (a claim, its
  reason, "so I like that"), merge them into one bullet, a short line in the owner's own words,
  citing every one of those sentences. Filler that makes no point of its own ("Couple of things.")
  gets no bullet: add its number to the nearest bullet's citation instead.
- AT MOST TWO LEVELS: a bullet, and sub-bullets under it. Never a third level.
- KEEP EVERY POINT. Merging sentences that make the same point is required; dropping a point is
  not allowed. Never turn a hedge ("maybe", "I think", "I guess") into a flat claim.
- Cite EVERY sentence number EXACTLY ONCE, in the one bullet where its main point went — never
  under two headings. Form: [S3, S7], each number individually, never a range like [S6-S9]. Use
  only numbers that appear below.

STYLE of anything the owner will read (the owner's rules):
- It is an OVERVIEW of what was said, in the owner's own key words. Never the whole rant, never a retelling.
- Each point has its answer or action baked in: say what is done, what to do, or what is still open. Do not invent an answer the transcript or the facts do not give; mark such a point open instead.
- Order by dependency and ease: clarifications and quick items first, then what depends on them. If neither applies, keep the owner's order.
- Reuse the same names for the same things every time, so they become familiar, and always name the context (the page, class, module or session) a point belongs to.
- Headings are big: "#" for the one subject, "##" for each part, "###" only when a part truly needs a split. Never "####" or smaller. Every heading starts with one fitting emoji icon.
- Under a heading: short titled lists. A status bullet starts with ✅ (done) or ⬜ (not done) when the status is known; otherwise a plain "-" bullet. Few emoji, never decoration.
- Every card cites the clean-sentence numbers it came from, like [S3, S7], each number individually.
Apply this to the headings and bullets of the outline.

Cleaned transcript:
"""
S1. So I think the microphone might be picking up some of your words.
S2. That thank you there, that's like the typical whisper.
S3. I didn't say that.
S4. That's a typical whisper, like when silent audio gets processed.
S5. So maybe it was just our, whenever, the detection mechanism that the microphone uses to actually send off the next audio sample, it's possible that it heard a bit or a piece or whatever from either what you said or just background noise or something, and then sends off little chunks of silence.
S6. That's what I would guess happened for the thank you.
S7. And then the "up things" comment was, I think it would stopped reading your previous message halfway through, and it had nothing to do with the words "up things."
S8. It mistranscribed it, but I think what's happening is because it's listening and speaking at the same time, then your words are being kind of — well, it's feedback.
S9. You're transcribing your own words.
S10. I don't know if there's an easy way around that.
S11. It's possible we could use sound canceling, essentially, to remove your spoken words from the audio.
S12. And I don't know the best way to do that.
S13. If you do it with full strength, then it's likely to suppress actual voice.
S14. Maybe you can suppress part of the audio or try to match the microphone audio that sounds similar or looks similar in waveform or whatever.
S15. I don't know.
S16. That gets really complicated, how to adjust the... and maybe it's just reducing the thresholds when you're speaking.
S17. It's also possible that configuring the thresholds dynamically — like right now, if my voice comes in loud and clear, it might reach a threshold way beyond what the minimum threshold is currently setting.
S18. And so moving that up towards just a higher minimum threshold for sounds could help.
S19. However, it might also cut off the beginning or end of words or something, where I'm not sure if that's the right way to do it — you could write that down.
S20. Yeah, I mean, so the V2 and the V3 are still there and kind of working.
S21. V2 doesn't have any live whisper transcriptions.
S22. V3 does, which is kind of cool.
S23. Yeah, I don't know if the timing of V3's kind of dimmed words
S24. So the dimmed words are now almost too strong.
S25. So there's not much of a difference between the dimmed words and the... I don't know if they're actually fully white, but they look almost near white.
S26. And so the spatial differentiation from the dimmed... anyway, just the muted needs to be a little bit more muted, I would say.
S27. Also, there's no paragraphs in these long dictations.
S28. So the current message right now is a single paragraph since your last message, which was your response to when I said thank you, you said you're welcome.
S29. So anyway, it's been one giant wall of text on V3.
S30. If I go back to V1, I think, okay, it's still a giant wall of text.
S31. So maybe it's using a similar algorithm.
S32. So for those, it's kind of where the placement thing came in.
S33. I'm not sure — the VS Code mastermind was having issues putting the fast assistant on pause.
S34. He said that it was refused or something, I'm not sure exactly what was going on there.
S35. Anyway, I don't know.
S36. I'm not sure if I've got the energy to continue working on this.
S37. I might just watch some TV and go to bed.
S38. Maybe ask the VS Code guy what is currently in flight and what he has planned for the future.
S39. Maybe I can give him a few more tips here.
"""

Output ONLY the Markdown described above (the H1, its H2s, and their bullets), nothing else.
